record.paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
record.original_question: Consider the class K_FNO^α of operators that can be approximated efficiently at rate α by Fourier neural operators, and let β★ denote the optimal algebraic minimax-rate exponent for learning that class in L^2_ϱ. The paper proves bounds showing β★ is at most 1/2 and approaches 1/2 as α grows. Is the exponent 1/2 actually sharp for these FNO-based operator classes, or can the true optimal exponent exceed the currently known upper-bound heuristic?

evidence.quote: Thm. 5 shows that the optimal algebraic minimax rate exponent is asymptotically 1/2 as α → ∞. The gap between the upper and lower bound in (10) for finite α is likely due to the ERM proof technique for the lower bound. It is of interest to determine whether the exponent 1/2 is sharp or not.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\varrho$ be a Borel probability measure on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal{X}$ and let $\mathcal{Y}$ be a separable Hilbert space. Consider learning an unknown operator $G:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$ from $n$ i.i.d. noisy input–output samples $(x_i,y_i)$, $x_i\sim\varrho$, $y_i=G(x_i)+\eta_i$, with the loss measured in $L^2_\varrho(\mathcal{X};\mathcal{Y})$.

For a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the Fourier-neural-operator approximation class $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$ as the set of operators $G$ such that there exists a sequence $\{G_M\}_{M\in\mathbb{N}}$ of Fourier neural operators of complexity (number of parameters / Fourier modes) at most $M$ with
$$\|G-G_M\|_{L^2_\varrho}\;\le\; C\, M^{-\alpha}.$$

For an estimator $\widehat G_n$ based on $n$ samples, define the minimax risk
$$R_n(\alpha)\;=\;\inf_{\widehat G_n}\sup_{G\in\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}}\mathbb{E}\,\|\widehat G_n-G\|^2_{L^2_\varrho},$$
and let the optimal algebraic minimax-rate exponent be
$$\beta^\star(\alpha)\;=\;\sup\{\beta\ge 0:\, R_n(\alpha)=O(n^{-\beta})\}.$$

It is known that $\beta^\star(\alpha)\le 1/2$ for all $\alpha$, and that $\beta^\star(\alpha)\to 1/2$ as $\alpha\to\infty$, while existing lower bounds (proved via empirical risk minimization arguments) leave a gap at finite $\alpha$.

Question. Determine whether the upper bound $\beta^\star(\alpha)=1/2$ is sharp for finite $\alpha>0$. Equivalently, does there exist a finite $\alpha$ and an estimator achieving an algebraic rate exponent strictly larger than the currently established lower-bound exponent, possibly attaining $1/2$, or can one prove a strict separation $\beta^\star(\alpha)<1/2$ for finite $\alpha$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on sharp minimax risk bounds for operator learning (e.g., arXiv:2512.17805, Dec 2025) develops information-theoretic lower bounds and upper bounds for Lipschitz operator classes between Hilbert spaces, but does not resolve whether the exponent 1/2 is sharp for finite-α FNO approximation classes. No source found that closes the gap between the upper and lower bounds for $\beta^\star(\alpha)$ at finite $\alpha$, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Sharp Minimax Risk Bounds for Operator Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Develops minimax lower and upper bounds for learning Lipschitz operators between separable Hilbert spaces; identifies regimes governed by covariance spectrum decay but does not pin down sharpness of the 1/2 exponent for FNO approximation classes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent minimax theory for operator learning leaves the sharpness of the 1/2 algebraic exponent for FNO classes unresolved at finite α.
